transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-25
Time: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 35 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood), Jordan Lee (Redwood Hiring Manager), Miguel Alvarez (Candidate)

Summary: quick recruiter screen to go over background, role fit, basics of interview loop, and next steps.

[00:00] Priya: Hi Miguel, thanks for taking the time, how are you?
[00:04] Miguel: Hey Priya, doing well thanks, excited to chat.
[00:07] Priya: Great, I'll do a quick intro — I'm Priya, recruiter here at Redwood Inference, and Jordan's the hiring manager for the infra team. We'll just walk through your background, why you're interested, a bit about the role and loop, and any questions you have. Sound good?
[00:20] Miguel: Yep that sounds perfect.
[00:23] Jordan: Hi Miguel, quick hello — I'm Jordan Lee, I lead the serving runtime team. Nice to meet you.
[00:28] Miguel: Nice to meet you too.

[00:30] Priya: Cool, could you give us a quick 2-3 minute summary of your current role at Acme Robotics and most relevant projects?
[00:36] Miguel: Sure. I'm a senior software engineer on the perception infra team, been there three years. Mostly building model serving infra for onboard systems, so lower-latency models on edge GPUs. I've done a lot with PyTorch, TorchScript, and some inference optimizations — like custom kernels and batching logic, plus KV cache style caching for repeated requests. I also worked on rolling upgrades and autoscaling for devices.
[01:05] Jordan: When you say custom kernels, is that C++/CUDA work or more high-level optimizations?
[01:09] Miguel: Mostly C++/CUDA, yeah. I helped port a couple ops to CUDA and tuned memory for peak throughput. Some of the quantization work was handled with custom runtime hooks, and we integrated a light-weight scheduler for request priorities.
[01:22] Jordan: Nice. Any experience with multi-tenant serving or routing policies?
[01:25] Miguel: Yeah, we had to multiplex models on the same devices for different clients, so I built isolation layers and a policy engine that would route by SLOs — it was fairly manual but similar idea to what folks call smart routing.

[01:36] Priya: Great — can you tell me what you're looking for next and why Redwood?
[01:40] Miguel: I'm looking for a role focused on inference infra at scale, with more focus on distributed serving and open models. I liked Redwood because of the emphasis on production-grade inference and the unified serving across hosted and private — that model routing and caching stuff really interests me.
[01:54] Priya: Awesome. A few logistics: what's your current title and base comp, and do you have any location or visa constraints?
[02:00] Miguel: Title is Senior Software Engineer. Base comp about 160k, equity is small. I'm authorized to work in the US — green card pending but I have employment authorization, so no sponsorship needed. I'm based in Austin, remote-first but open to occasional travel.
[02:16] Priya: Thanks. Our target range for this level is around the 150–190k base depending on experience, plus equity and benefits. We'll confirm final range if we move forward.

[02:26] Jordan: Quick technical questions — what's your latency/throughput tradeoff experience? Example: how did you handle batching to avoid tail latency?
[02:33] Miguel: We used adaptive batching with token limits and a timeout threshold; for critical requests we bypassed batching and put them on a fast path. We also used prefix caching for repeated sequences which reduced tokens in hot paths. Occasionally there were jitter issues in the scheduler so we added jitter smoothing.
[02:51] Jordan: Sounds familiar — have you instrumented per-model token cost or kept token-level accounting?
[02:55] Miguel: We had rough accounting, mostly at request-level. We didn't have the per-token granularity early on, but added it later for cost reporting. Some of the terminology I heard in Redwood talks — KV cache and continuous batching — maps to things I've done, although sometimes terms differ.
[03:12] Priya: Totally. For the interview loop: typical flow is tech screen (pairing), system design with a senior engineer, and then an onsite with a couple more pairing sessions. We'll also have a short take-home coding challenge (2-4 hours) for infra/optimization tasks. Does that timeline work?
[03:27] Miguel: Yeah, that fits. 2-4 hours is fine.

[03:30] Priya: How soon could you do a technical screen? Jordan has availability next week most afternoons.
[03:34] Miguel: I can do next Thursday afternoon or Friday morning.
[03:37] Jordan: Let's tentatively put Thursday 3pm, I'll follow up with a calendar invite.

[03:42] Priya: Do you have any questions about the role or team?
[03:45] Miguel: Yeah — how big is the serving runtime team and what's the main language/stack?
[03:49] Jordan: We're about 8 engineers on the runtime team, plus close collaboration with infra and SRE. Primary language is C++ for hot-path kernels, Python for orchestration, and we use a mix of PyTorch and ONNX for models. We deploy on k8s for dedicated/private setups and have internal autoscaling.
[04:07] Miguel: Cool. Do you do on-prem or VPC deployments often?
[04:10] Jordan: Both — customers use hosted, dedicated GPU pools, and private VPC options for compliance. You'd likely touch all three at some point.

[04:18] Miguel: Sounds perfect. I also wanted to ask about the take-home — is it open-book? And are we allowed to reuse libraries?
[04:23] Priya: Yes open-book, you can use libraries. It's focused on system design and optimization rather than reinventing algorithms. We'll share details and a starter repo link.

[04:32] Miguel: Great. One more: what's the typical onboarding for new hires on the runtime team?
[04:36] Jordan: Two-week ramp with pairing, reading docs and small bugfixes, then a feature project in month one. We'll assign a buddy and have doc checklists for infra.

[04:45] Priya: Okay, final logistics — are you interviewing other companies or timeline constraints?
[04:49] Miguel: I have a final loop with another company in 2 weeks, so I hope to move fairly quickly.
[04:55] Priya: Understood, we'll try to accelerate. I'll send JD, interview loop, and the take-home repo link after this call. Also please share any specific compensation expectations if 160k base isn't in line.

[05:08] Miguel: 160k base is my current comp; I'd like to be in the 170–190k range depending on equity.
[05:15] Priya: Noted. Any questions about visa / relocation?
[05:18] Miguel: No, I can work remote from Austin and travel as needed.

[05:22] Priya: Great. We'll follow up with next steps and calendar invites. Thanks for your time Miguel.
[05:27] Miguel: Thanks Priya, thank you Jordan.
[05:30] Jordan: Thanks Miguel, talk soon.

[05:34] End of recording.

Notes: transcription has small errors (some technical terms slightly mis-heard). Shared artifacts to be sent: link to JD (doc: /hiring/roles/runtime-senior-se.json), take-home repo link (git: https://git.redwood-internal/recruiting/runtime-challenge), interview loop schedule (calendar invite).
